sections.h2: Why is Bloomington a steady housing market compared with other Illinois cities?
sections.html:
Bloomington is the McLean County seat in central Illinois, laid out in 1831 after the county was created in December 1830. It grew from a settlement called Keg Grove, later Blooming Grove, and a fire in 1900 destroyed most of downtown, which was quickly rebuilt from local architects' designs. Insurance did the most to shape the modern city: State Farm was founded here in June 1922, and the city's 2018 financial report lists State Farm as its largest employer, followed by Illinois State University in neighboring Normal, Country Financial, McLean County Unit District No. 5, Carle Bromenn Medical Center and OSF St. Joseph Medical Center.

Bloomington covers 27.24 square miles, and its Census count rose from 76,610 in 2010 to 78,680 in 2020. Those employers draw buyers from the Bloomington-Normal area as a whole, so a listing here is read next to Normal houses too.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Bloomington homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 78,804 residents for July 1, 2025, up 0.1 percent from the April 2020 base of 78,688. Close to half of adults age 25 and over hold a bachelor's degree, and the average commute is short.

sections.h2: Which school districts and amenities shape Bloomington buyer interest?
sections.html:
Two public districts cover the city. Bloomington Public Schools District 87 serves the interior with Bloomington High School, Bloomington Junior High and six elementary schools (Oakland, Washington, Bent, Irving, Sheridan and Stevenson) plus a preschool. Growth pushed the city well into McLean County Unit District No. 5, which runs Normal Community High School and Normal Community West High School and now enrolls most of its students from Bloomington itself. A small part of the city lies in Olympia Community Unit School District 16, and Central Catholic High School is a private option.

  • Parks: the Parks and Recreation Department maintains over 1,100 acres across 44 park sites and three golf courses, plus Miller Park Zoo.
  • Trails: the 24-mile Constitution Trail follows former railroad right-of-way through much of the city.
  • Colleges: Illinois Wesleyan University (founded 1850) is in the city, and Illinois State University is in Normal.
  • Culture: the Bloomington Center for the Performing Arts anchors the downtown Cultural District.

Because the school district can differ from one block to the next, confirm the district for your address before writing the listing description.

sections.h2: How do Interstates, rail and air access affect Bloomington sellers?
sections.html:
Interstates 39, 55 and 74 intersect at Bloomington, and US 51, US 150 and Illinois Route 9 also pass through. Historic US 66 once ran directly through downtown and later on a bypass to the east.

Amtrak serves the area from Uptown Station in neighboring Normal, with five trains in each direction daily between St. Louis and Chicago, and Greyhound and Burlington Trailways add bus links. Central Illinois Regional Airport on Route 9 has flights on Delta, American Eagle, Frontier and Allegiant. Connect Transit runs 13 fixed bus routes. These details matter when you market to out-of-town buyers or employees transferring in.

sections.h2: What must Bloomington owners know if the house is a rental?
sections.html:
Anyone who owns residential rental property inside the city limits must register it with the city and hold a Certificate of Inspection before renting or leasing a unit. This affects sellers because the city's rules shape what a buyer inherits.

  • Registration costs $65 per building, plus $5 per rental unit in buildings of three or more units, and each owned condo needs its own registration.
  • Registrations run until December 31 each year and cannot be transferred to new owners, so a buyer must register on their own.
  • The first inspection is included in the registration fee. Follow-up inspections are $100 each and a missed inspection costs $75.
  • Owners get at least 15 days' notice, and inspectors enforce the International Property Maintenance Code, the Fire Code and other city ordinances.
  • A building rated fair may be required to post a $5,000 letter of credit or pledged account until it receives a passing rating.
  • Violations not fixed by the reinspection date lead to a court appearance and possible court costs.

Owners who rent short term face a 6.0 percent city Short Term Rental Tax on stays under 30 days, with remittance due by the 25th of the following month and a 5 percent penalty for late payments. Those operators must also register the unit annually in the rental program. Sellers of a rental should settle any unpaid tax or inspection issue before closing. A cash buyer will often take on a tenant-occupied or violation-heavy property as-is, which can avoid a repair-and-reinspect cycle.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded in McLean County?
sections.html:
The McLean County Clerk's office handles recording at 115 E. Washington Street, Bloomington, and its Predictable Recording Fee Schedule effective July 1, 2023 lists a standard document at $61.00. Documents exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee, such as government filings and powers of attorney, are $41.00, and a non-standard document is $75.00. A document counts as non-standard if it uses legal- or ledger-size paper or has six or more PIN or related-document references. Recorded documents must be originals or certified copies. Certified copies cost $18.00 and additional copies $1.00 per page.

The county's phone for recording is (309) 888-5170. The state transfer declaration and any transfer tax are separate from the recording fee. Your title company will collect them at closing, so ask for an itemized settlement statement.

sections.h2: How does McLean County handle assessment complaints and tax bills in Bloomington?
sections.html:
Taxpayers have 30 days from the publication date shown for their township to file an assessment complaint with the Board of Review, and a late complaint will not be heard. For 2026, the county table shows the Bloomington and City of Bloomington townships published on September 29, 2026 with a filing deadline of October 29, 2026, so that window has closed. The equalization factors for those townships were 1.0534 and 1.0385.

The county uses Form PTAX-230 for non-farm complaints. The assessment is based on the past three years' market value before January 1 of the assessment year, with a multiplier applied to bring the statutory assessment to 33.33 percent. The City of Bloomington Township Assessor keeps property record cards and a lookup tool, and the Board of Review office can be reached at (309) 888-5132. For future cycles, check the county's table for your township's publication and deadline dates, and ask the County Treasurer for installment dates and a payoff figure before closing.

faqs.q: Can a new owner use the previous owner's Bloomington rental registration?
faqs.a: No. Bloomington's rental program says registrations cannot be transferred to new owners. A buyer who plans to rent must register the building, pay the registration fee and pass inspection.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in McLean County?
faqs.a: The county's schedule effective July 1, 2023 lists $61.00 for a standard document and $75.00 for a non-standard one. Fees can change, so confirm with the County Clerk before sending payment.

faqs.q: Did the 2026 Bloomington appeal window close?
faqs.a: Yes. McLean County's table shows a filing deadline of October 29, 2026 for the Bloomington and City of Bloomington townships, and late complaints are not heard. The same 30-days-from-publication rule applies in later years.

faqs.q: Is the short-term rental tax applied to every Bloomington short-term stay?
faqs.a: The city's FAQ applies a 6.0 percent tax to rentals of less than 30 days and lists no exemptions. Operators who use a listing site must still register each property and file monthly certification forms.

faqs.q: Does a cash sale remove the need to fix rental violations in Bloomington?
faqs.a: The city's rules still apply to whoever owns the building, but a cash buyer may agree to buy as-is and handle repairs and reinspection after closing. Settle fees or court matters tied to your ownership first, and get any sale terms in writing.
